successCriteria.description: A new knex migration under `migrations/` adds a nullable `reverses_request_id` text column to `leave_requests`, a self-referencing FK to `leave_requests.id`, and a UNIQUE index on `reverses_request_id`; `exports.down` drops the index, the FK and the column. The migration applies cleanly against real PostgreSQL (up then down).

The migration file's comment records the BINDING rule that any aggregation summing `requested_days` MUST filter on `reverses_request_id IS NULL`, because a reversal row copies the original's `requestedDays` verbatim (never re-derived, never zeroed).

`LeaveRequest` in `src/modules/leave/leave.model.ts` exposes `reversesRequestId: string | null` as its LAST field, with the other 14 fields unchanged in name, type and order; `CreateLeaveRequestInput` remains `Omit<LeaveRequest, 'id'>` so it now requires `reversesRequestId`.

`PgLeaveRequestRepository` carries `reverses_request_id` end-to-end: it is in the SELECT column list, the row interface, the row mapper, and the INSERT column/value list (15 values); a created row round-trips a non-null `reversesRequestId` and an ordinary row round-trips `null`.

`ILeaveRepository` declares `findByReversesRequestId(reversesRequestId: string, client?: PoolClient): Promise<LeaveRequest | null>` and `PgLeaveRequestRepository` implements it, returning the matching reversal row when present and `null` when absent (never throwing).
`npm run build` (tsc) is clean and the existing Jest suite still passes with no test-file changes.

constraints: Only three files change: the new migration under `migrations/`, `src/modules/leave/leave.model.ts`, and `src/modules/leave/leave.repository.ts`. No service, route, controller, index.ts, shared-types, web, or test file is touched.

The canonical `LeaveRequest` shape is id, employeeId, leaveTypeCode, startDate, endDate, requestedDays, reason, status, approverId, approvalComment, submittedAt, decidedAt, cancelledBy, cancelledAt, reversesRequestId. No field may be added, renamed, split, reordered or retyped; `reversesRequestId` is appended last.
`reversesRequestId` is consumed by the `leave` module only and must NOT be promoted to `src/shared/types/`.
`reversesRequestId` must NOT be added to the repository's update-field map: the column is set at INSERT time only and is never updated. `update` must not be able to write it.

Every repository method keeps the optional trailing `PoolClient` parameter and the private `db(client)` fallback to the shared pool; the repository never issues BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK. The new lookup method follows the same signature convention.

The migration targets PostgreSQL (the declared database) and follows the existing migration conventions: knex `exports.up`/`exports.down`, alter-table style, and a header comment recording the binding aggregation rule.
The repository must not throw on a missing reversal row — it returns `null`; error semantics (e.g. ConflictError) belong to the service in a later phase.
Strict TypeScript: no `any` (use `unknown` with type guards), strict null checks; all database access stays behind the repository interface (GP-001).
outOfScope: The `LeaveService.cancel` reversal branch (GP-008) — inserting the new CANCELLED reversal row, the balance release, the CANCEL audit and the notification — is Phase 2 and must not be built here.
The web `LeaveRequestView.reversesRequestId` field and any read-path/route change are Phase 3.
The reversal unit test and smoke assertion are Phase 4; no test file changes this phase.
Any change to `src/shared/types/index.ts` (canonical enums, `UpdateLeaveRequestDto`, `requestedDays` helper) — unchanged this phase.

ambiguities.description: The UNIQUE index on `reverses_request_id` is described as "partial/unique". A plain UNIQUE index on a nullable column already permits many NULLs in PostgreSQL, so a partial index (`WHERE reverses_request_id IS NOT NULL`) is functionally equivalent; the choice affects only the DDL shape.
options: Plain UNIQUE index on the nullable column
Partial UNIQUE index with WHERE reverses_request_id IS NOT NULL

ambiguities.description: The migration timestamp/filename is unspecified beyond `<timestamp>_add_reverses_request_id_to_leave_requests.js`; the chosen timestamp must sort after the existing migrations.
The FK on `reverses_request_id` has no stated ON DELETE behaviour; the initial schema's other self-referencing FKs (e.g. `manager_id`) use the default (NO ACTION).

entityInvariants.invariant: `reversesRequestId` is null for every ordinary request and non-null only on a reversal row, where it equals the id of the original APPROVED request it reverses. It is set at INSERT time only and is never updated afterwards.

A reversal row is born CANCELLED and is terminal/inert: it never transitions again, reserves nothing, and is never itself the target of a second reversal. At most one reversal row may exist per original request — enforced by the UNIQUE index on `reverses_request_id`.
Nullable text column with a self-referencing FK to `leave_requests.id` and a UNIQUE index; the FK and index are dropped before the column in `exports.down`.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: No authorization — repository layer; callers enforce RBAC.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Read-only lookup; returns the matching LeaveRequest or null when absent. Never throws for a missing row — the service decides error semantics (ConflictError) in a later phase.
Inserts all 15 columns including `reverses_request_id` and returns the persisted row. A UNIQUE violation on `reverses_request_id` surfaces as a database error (the backstop for a double reversal).

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The repository's snake_case↔camelCase mapping, SELECT column list, row interface and INSERT list must stay in lockstep with the canonical `LeaveRequest` field order and names — `reverses_request_id` is appended last in each, matching the model.

The migration's column name, nullability, FK target and UNIQUE index must match the conceptual `leave_requests` specification (nullable `reverses_request_id`, FK to `leave_requests.id`, UNIQUE index) and the existing initial-schema conventions.
The alter-table migration style (knex `alterTable`, `exports.up`/`exports.down`, header comment) must match the existing password_hash migration.
The repository interface must be declared inline in `leave.repository.ts` (the balance convention), not in a separate `leave.repository.interface.ts` file.
The new lookup method's signature and client-threading convention must match the existing repository methods (optional trailing `PoolClient`, private `db(client)` fallback, no BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK).

integrationPoints.why: The reversal branch consumes `LeaveRequest.reversesRequestId` and `ILeaveRepository.findByReversesRequestId`; the field and method must exist with the exact names/types this phase delivers.
Re-exports `LeaveRequest` and `ILeaveRepository`; the added field and method flow through unchanged — no edit required, but the public surface must remain consistent.

The `FakeLeaveRepository` must satisfy the extended `ILeaveRepository` (gaining `findByReversesRequestId`) and fixtures must supply `reversesRequestId`; the interface shape this phase fixes is what the fake must match.
